purpose: Evidence-backed hypothesis registry for improving M1 short-term reversal rather than random formula mining.

hypotheses.mechanism: One-month losers can partially reverse over the next month.
hypotheses.implication: Retain M1's core recent-loss signal as the anchor.

sources.title: Short-Term Reversals and Longer-Term Momentum around the World: Theory and Evidence
Cross-Section of Stock Returns Around the World in the Early Twentieth Century

hypotheses.mechanism: Short-term reversal returns are related to liquidity provision; volatility and liquidity conditions change the strength and persistence of reversals.
hypotheses.implication: Test both a safety liquidity filter and a contrarian illiquidity-tilt, rather than assuming one direction.

sources.title: Reversals and the Returns to Liquidity Provision
Reversal returns and expected returns from liquidity provision: Evidence from emerging markets

hypotheses.mechanism: The reversal/momentum relation changes with turnover and the stock's position relative to its 52-week high.
hypotheses.implication: Use 52-week-high distance as a conditioning variable instead of treating all M1 losers as equivalent.

sources.title: Short-term momentum and reversals, turnover, and a stock’s price-to-52-week-high ratio

hypotheses.mechanism: Reversal strength can increase in volatile/liquidity-stressed states, while extreme volatility can also raise tail risk.
hypotheses.implication: Test volatility as a signal conditioner and separately test exposure reduction in market-stress regimes.

sources.title: Reversals and the Returns to Liquidity Provision

hypotheses.mechanism: Very short-term reversal can coexist with longer-horizon momentum; the transition means a recent loser can either be a temporary dislocation or a persistent downtrend.
hypotheses.implication: Test a medium-horizon trend floor to avoid automatically buying structural downtrends.

sources.title: Short-Term Reversals and Longer-Term Momentum around the World: Theory and Evidence

design_rules: No future return may influence the month being traded.
Forward monthly return requires the next calendar month to exist.
Candidate selection is frozen before OOS and HOLDOUT.
Costs are stress-tested at 20/40/60 bps per one-way turnover unit.
Regime exposure changes incur explicit turnover costs.
A positive OOS result alone is insufficient for promotion; blind HOLDOUT and robustness are mandatory.
